theme: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank

candidates.name: crux-top-lists
candidates.what_it_holds: Monthly CSV.gz snapshots (columns: origin, rank) of Chrome's top ~1M sites derived from Google's public CrUX BigQuery dataset. Rank is bucketed (1000/10K/100K/1M) by pageload volume, both global and country-specific lists, cached under data/global/ back to roughly 2018 (monthly releases, second Tuesday of month). Current file at raw.githubusercontent.com/zakird/crux-top-lists/main/data/global/current.csv.gz. CITATION.cff present.
candidates.why_useful: airbnb.com's CrUX popularity-rank bucket over time is a free, long-running proxy for site-visit volume/engagement (gap #5, engagement/web-traffic). Monthly history since 2018 lets you build a point-in-time-ish visitation trend and compare against nights/GBV seasonality; also covers competitor domains (booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com) for relative-share reads.
candidates.size_hint: CSV.gz per month, ~1M rows each, chunked
candidates.license: Data under Google CrUX Dataset Terms; repo code likely permissive (check LICENSE file)

candidates.name: crux-cache
candidates.what_it_holds: Cached CrUX data for 'all ~18M origins tracked by CrUX' with popularity rank buckets, as CSV files chunked to 25MB for GitHub, refreshed monthly by automation. MIT-licensed repo code; underlying data under CrUX Dataset Terms.
candidates.why_useful: Broader origin coverage than crux-top-lists (18M vs 1M origins) — could catch smaller competitor/adjacent sites (Sonder, Vacasa, Hipcamp) not in the top-1M cut, still keyed to airbnb.com rank history for engagement trend (gap #5).
candidates.time_coverage: monthly, ongoing (35 commits at time of check)

candidates.name: CloudflareRadarKit
candidates.what_it_holds: Typed Swift client library wrapping the Cloudflare Radar API (internet traffic volume, outage, BGP, and related network metrics) for iOS 17+/macOS 14+. No committed dataset — a one-call API client for pulling Cloudflare Radar's public traffic/ranking endpoints (Cloudflare also publishes a domain popularity ranking via Radar).
candidates.why_useful: Cloudflare Radar exposes a domain-ranking endpoint and traffic-share time series that could stand in for web-engagement proxies (gap #5) and AI-crawler/bot traffic share (gap #19); this client shows the API is free and scriptable even though the client itself is Swift (a Python client would need to be written against the same public endpoints).
candidates.time_coverage: live API, historical ranges depend on Radar API

candidates.name: mcp-cloudflare-radar
candidates.what_it_holds: An MCP (model-context-protocol) server wrapping Cloudflare Radar's API for traffic, attack (DDoS), BGP routing, and internet-quality metrics — a thin API bridge, not a stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Another confirmation the Radar API is queryable for domain/traffic-share data feeding gap #5/#19; low incremental value beyond showing endpoint coverage (traffic, BGP, quality).

candidates.name: cloudflare-radar (isthiam)
candidates.what_it_holds: 'Empirical analysis of global internet security across 252 countries using Cloudflare Radar API data from 2025-2026' — implies pulled and possibly committed country-level Radar metrics (traffic/security) for a broad country set, plus analysis code.
candidates.why_useful: If country-level traffic/attack data is committed rather than just pulled live, it gives a recent (2025-2026) point-in-time snapshot of internet activity by country that could proxy regional online travel-shopping intensity (gap #5) alongside FX/consumer-strength splits (NA/EMEA/LatAm/APAC).

candidates.name: top-1m-domains (PeterDaveHello)
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated list of download links (not committed data) to eight top-domain ranking services: Alexa (historical), Cisco Umbrella, Majestic, BuiltWith, Statvoo, DomCop, Tranco, and Cloudflare Radar top domains — mostly .csv.zip direct-download URLs to each vendor's own host.
candidates.why_useful: One-stop index of where to pull Tranco/Majestic/Cisco Umbrella/Cloudflare top-1M domain CSVs (each free, updated daily/weekly) for building an airbnb.com and competitor-domain rank time series (gap #5) — a navigation aid rather than a dataset itself.
candidates.time_coverage: current snapshots only (links point to daily/weekly vendor feeds, not history)

candidates.name: top-1m-domains (rix4uni)
candidates.what_it_holds: Similar curated compilation of top-1-million-domain list sources ('Alexa alternatives') — links to Tranco, Majestic, Cisco Umbrella etc., security-research oriented (recon/bug-bounty use case).
candidates.why_useful: Redundant with PeterDaveHello/top-1m-domains but confirms multiple maintained indices of the same free rank feeds; low incremental value beyond that repo.

candidates.name: top-sites-ranking-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Go-based API service (MIT licensed, 31 commits) tagged 'tranco', apparently serving/normalizing top-site ranking data (likely wrapping Tranco's list) behind a small API; README content was not retrievable in the fetch, so exact source coverage is unconfirmed.
candidates.why_useful: Potential lightweight self-hosted wrapper for querying Tranco rank of airbnb.com and peers programmatically, but unverified scope — flagged for a follow-up direct README read before relying on it.

candidates.name: cc-webgraph
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Common Crawl toolkit (Java + PySpark, Apache-2.0, 176 commits) to construct host-level and domain-level web graphs from Common Crawl crawl data and compute harmonic-centrality / PageRank-style rank scores using the WebGraph framework. No pre-built data files shipped in-repo; users run it against Common Crawl's own webgraph release files (hosted separately at commoncrawl.org/web-graphs, updated per crawl) to produce rank output files like `<graph>-ranks.txt.gz`.
candidates.why_useful: This is the actual method behind 'Common Crawl host-graph rank' named in the theme brief — it lets you derive a host-level authority/rank score for airbnb.com and competitor domains from Common Crawl's periodically released host graphs (several per year, going back to ~2017), a free alternative to Tranco/Majestic that is already partially in scope given we hold a Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (existing holding). Directly extends what we already hold rather than duplicating it.
candidates.time_coverage: per Common Crawl webgraph releases, ~2017-present, several/year
candidates.size_hint: toolkit only; source webgraphs are multi-GB, hosted externally at commoncrawl.org/web-graphs
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: extends existing Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com; different data product (host-graph rank vs CDX index)

candidates.name: crawlgraph-datasets
candidates.what_it_holds: CSV/JSON datasets of domains linking into specific competitor-tool categories (SEO tools 9,687 domains, CRMs 9,910, AI agent frameworks 7,508, fintech apps 12,106), each row carrying a 'CrawlGraph authority score' (0-100) derived from Common Crawl's open hyperlink graph (~120M domains, 4.4B links, refreshed quarterly, queried via DuckDB). Free to reuse with attribution; 4 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Demonstrates a working, quarterly-refreshed Common Crawl host-graph authority-score pipeline (queryable via DuckDB, which the team already uses) that could be re-pointed at travel/OTA domains (airbnb.com, booking.com, vrbo.com, expedia.com) to build a backlink-authority proxy for site prominence — marginal fit since the shipped categories are unrelated (SEO/CRM/fintech/AI tools), but the method and data source are directly reusable.
candidates.size_hint: 4 CSV/JSON files, several thousand rows each
candidates.license: free with attribution (CrawlGraph); underlying data Common Crawl open data
candidates.last_activity: 4 commits, recent (Common Crawl quarterly refresh cadence implies 2025-2026 activity)

candidates.name: webgraph (LAW / vigna)
candidates.what_it_holds: The core WebGraph framework (Java) for compressing and analyzing large web graphs and computing rank measures (PageRank, harmonic centrality) — the underlying library that Common Crawl's cc-webgraph and the LAW group's Common Crawl host-rank releases are built on. No data committed, just the compression/ranking library.
candidates.why_useful: Foundational dependency for anyone wanting to reproduce or verify Common Crawl host-graph rank numbers rather than a data source itself; low direct value beyond method provenance.
candidates.license: unspecified in fetch (check repo, historically LGPL/Apache dual)

candidates.name: similarweb-scraper-public (name approximate, via Apify)
candidates.what_it_holds: Listed on GitHub's 'similarweb' topic as extracting website traffic and ranking data via the Apify scraping platform (i.e., an Apify actor wrapper). Method-only, no committed Similarweb dataset for airbnb.com; relies on Apify's hosted scraper for the live pull.
candidates.why_useful: One of several small scrapers indicating Similarweb visit-estimate data (visits, bounce rate, traffic-source mix, top competitors) can be pulled for airbnb.com/booking.com/vrbo.com without a paid Similarweb subscription, feeding gap #5 web-traffic estimates — but per repo rules this is a method to catalogue and NOT run against Similarweb's own terms without a human sign-off (scraping a third-party site, not airbnb.com itself, so lower ToS sensitivity than scraping airbnb.com directly, but still worth a human check).

candidates.name: similarweb-traffic-data-python (name approximate)
candidates.what_it_holds: Listed on the 'similarweb' GitHub topic as a 'Python scraper for traffic data without subscription' — a method-only repo scraping Similarweb's free public site-overview pages for visit-count estimates, engagement metrics, and top-competitor lists.
candidates.why_useful: Same class of value as similarweb-scraper-public: a free-tier method to get Similarweb's visit-estimate/rank numbers for airbnb.com and OTA peers programmatically for gap #5. Multiple independent repos of this shape suggest the free Similarweb overview page is a stable, scrapeable source, though individual repos churn/break often (Similarweb changes its page structure) — verify freshness before relying on any one.

cloudflare radar api python client github (WebSearch, blocked)
chrome ux report crux top rank github dataset (WebSearch, blocked)
notes: WebSearch tool returned 'session has used its web search budget (200 of 200)' on the very first call in this session — apparently a shared per-session budget already exhausted by other concurrent scout agents before this scout's turn ran. Worked around it entirely via WebFetch against GitHub topic pages (github.com/topics/<tag>) and direct repo URLs, which does not use the WebSearch quota. This surfaced good candidates but is narrower than a full web search sweep (no Kaggle/Zenodo/HuggingFace/blog-post discovery was possible). A `github.com/search?q=...` fetch was rate-limited (HTTP 429, retry-after 3600s) — GitHub's own search UI throttles unauthenticated WebFetch hits, so topic pages (github.com/topics/X) were the reliable channel instead. Majestic Million has literally no GitHub topic tag and no dedicated repo found (it's typically consumed as a paid/free daily CSV download directly from majestic.com, not mirrored on GitHub) — flag this as a real gap: nobody mirrors Majestic Million on GitHub as far as this pass found. Tranco itself is best obtained via its own official Python package/API (pypi 'tranco'), not found as a browsable GitHub data mirror in this pass (official generation-code repo guess DistriNet/tranco-list-generation 404'd — likely wrong org/name, worth a retry with proper search once quota resets). Suggest a follow-up scout re-run the WebSearch-based queries (site:github.com tranco historical rank data csv; site:github.com majestic million mirror; awesome-lists for 'web analytics OSINT') once the session's WebSearch budget resets, and also check pypi/GitHub for the official 'tranco' Python client repo and 'SEOlyzer'/'openrank' style Common Crawl PageRank mirrors (e.g. webdatacommons.org hyperlink graph, and the LAW group's own periodic Common Crawl host-rank CSV releases at law.di.unimi.it, which may be pointer-to-external-host candidates worth recording even without a GitHub repo).
